# Task 1: Indel Calling - Create a Slurm Job
## Illumina
```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=msalomon_1816
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=6:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=indel_calling_illumina
#SBATCH --output=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/indel_calling_illumina_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/indel_calling_illumina_%j.err

source ~/.bashrc
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
conda activate /project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/trgn515

ref_genome=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/ref_genome/GRCh38/genome.fa
input_bam=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_1/mapping/illumina_chr20.realigned.bam
out_dir=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/02_indels/illumina
output=$out_dir/illumina.chr20.indels.filtered.vcf.gz
mkdir -p $out_dir

bcftools mpileup --threads 4 \
    -f $ref_genome \
    -a AD,ADF,ADR,DP,SP \
    -q 0 \
    -Q 0 \
    -Ou \
    $input_bam \
| bcftools call \
    -m \
    -v \
    -V snps \
    -Ou \
| bcftools norm \
    -f $ref_genome \
    -m -any \
    -Ou \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinMQ'   -e 'MQ < 20' \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinQUAL' -e 'QUAL < 20' \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinDP'   -e 'FMT/DP < 20' \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinAD' \
    -e '(FMT/GT ~ "1/1" && FMT/AD[:1] < 10) || (FMT/GT ~ "0/1" && FMT/AD[:1] < 5)' \
    -Oz -o $output --threads 4

tabix -p vcf $output
```

## Pacbio
```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=msalomon_1816
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=indel_calling_pacbio
#SBATCH --output=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/indel_calling_pacbio_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/indel_calling_pacbio_%j.err

set -euo pipefail

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate /project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/clair

export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

which bcftools
which tabix
bcftools --version

model=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/clair/Clair3/models/hifi
ref_genome=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/ref_genome/GRCh38/genome.fa
input_bam=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_1/mapping/pacbio.chr20.sorted.bam
out_dir=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/02_indels/pacbio

mkdir -p $out_dir

run_clair3.sh \
--bam_fn=$input_bam \
--ref_fn=$ref_genome \
--threads=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK \
--platform="hifi" \
--model_path=$model \
--output=$out_dir

bcftools view \
--types indels \
$out_dir/merge_output.vcf.gz \
-Ou \
| bcftools norm \
--threads $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK \
-f $ref_genome \
-Ou \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinDP'  -e 'FMT/DP < 20' \
| bcftools filter -m+ -s 'MinAD'  -e '(FMT/GT ~ "1/1" && FMT/AD[0:1] < 10) || (FMT/GT ~ "0/1" && FMT/AD[0:1] < 5)' \
-Oz --threads $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK \
-o $out_dir/pacbio.chr20.indels.filtered.vcf.gz

tabix -p vcf $out_dir/pacbio.chr20.indels.filtered.vcf.gz
```

# Task 2: Structural Variant calling 
## 1. Create a slurm job
### illumina-mapping with GRCh37
```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=msalomon_1816
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=sv_illumina_delly
#SBATCH --output=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/sv_illumina_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/sv_illumina_%j.err

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate /project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/trgn515

FASTQ1=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_1/fastq/hg200_illumina_chr20_1.fastq.gz
FASTQ2=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_1/fastq/hg200_illumina_chr20_2.fastq.gz

REF_BWA=/project2/biodb/genomes/Homo_sapiens/NCBI/build37.2/Sequence/BWAIndex/genome.fa
REF_FASTA=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/ref_genome/GRCh37/genome.fa

OUTDIR=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/03_sv/illumina_chr20
mkdir -p $OUTDIR

SAMPLE=hg200

flowcell=$(zcat "$FASTQ1" | head -n1 | cut -d':' -f3)
lane=$(zcat "$FASTQ1" | head -n1 | cut -d':' -f4)

RGID=${flowcell}.${lane}
PU=${flowcell}.${lane}.${SAMPLE}
PL=ILLUMINA

bwa mem -t 8 \
  -R "@RG\tID:${RGID}\tPU:${PU}\tPL:${PL}\tSM:${SAMPLE}" \
  "$REF_BWA" \
  "$FASTQ1" \
  "$FASTQ2" \
  | samtools view -bS - \
  | samtools sort -@ 8 -o "$OUTDIR/illumina_chr20.GRCh37.sorted.bam"
samtools index "$OUTDIR/illumina_chr20.GRCh37.sorted.bam"
```

# Task 3: Discusssion of detection methods 
## 1. Why can we use general variant calling software that relies on alignment statistics (eg: bcftools, GATK…) to detect small Indels, but require specialized algorithms to detect large SVs? 
* Bcftools and GATK detect variants by looking at base quality, mapping quality and the number of reads contribute to a variant at a position in the alignment to the reference genome. 
* Small indels are a local sequence changes. Small insertions and deletions are shorter than the read length, so they can be completely contained within a single read. When mapping to the reference genome, we can directly detect how many base pairs are deleted from the alignment.
* In contrast, large structural variants involve rearrangement of an entire genomic segments, such as large deletions, insertions, or duplications. Large SVs cannot be fully represented within a single read alignment, so they require specialized algorithms to detect them.

# Task 4 - Attach your code to calculate the FN and FP to the assignment. Briefly explain how the code works and why it calculates FN and FP. (10pts)
## Illumina
```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=msalomon_1816
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=illumina_benchmarking
#SBATCH --output=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/illumina_benchmarking%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/illumina_benchmarking%j.err

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate /project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/trgn515

IN=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/03_sv/illumina_chr20
BENCH=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/benchmark/HG002_GRCh37_SVs_Tier1_v0.6.vcf.gz
GENOME=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/ref_genome/GRCh37/GRCh37.genome
OUT=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/benchmark/illumina
mkdir -p $OUT

bcftools view -i 'INFO/SVTYPE="DEL" || INFO/SVTYPE="INS"' \
$IN/illumina_chr20.sv.pass.vcf.gz \
| bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\n' \
| bedtools slop -g $GENOME -b 100 \
> $OUT/sample.bed

bcftools view -i 'INFO/SVTYPE="DEL" || INFO/SVTYPE="INS"' \
$BENCH \
| bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\n' \
| bedtools slop -g $GENOME -b 100 \
> $OUT/benchmark.bed

#TP
bedtools intersect \
-a $OUT/sample.bed \
-b $OUT/benchmark.bed \
-f 0.5 -r -u \
> $OUT/TP.bed

# FP
bedtools intersect \
-a $OUT/sample.bed \
-b $OUT/benchmark.bed \
-f 0.5 -r -v \
> $OUT/FP.bed

# FN
bedtools intersect \
-a $OUT/benchmark.bed \
-b $OUT/sample.bed \
-f 0.5 -r -v \
> $OUT/FN.bed
```

```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=msalomon_1816
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1

#SBATCH --mem=32G
```

```sh
#SBATCH --output=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/ont_benchmarking%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/logs/ont_benchmarking%j.err

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate /project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/conda_env/trgn515

IN=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/03_sv/ont_chr20GRCh37
SAMPLE_VCF=$IN/ont_chr20.sniffles.pass.vcf.gz
BENCH=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/benchmark/HG002_GRCh37_SVs_Tier1_v0.6.vcf.gz
GENOME=/project2/msalomon_1816/trgn_515/2_sv/ref_genome/GRCh37/GRCh37.genome
OUT=/project2/msalomon_1816/ranzhu/assignment_2/benchmark/ont
mkdir -p $OUT

bcftools view -i 'INFO/SVTYPE="DEL" || INFO/SVTYPE="INS"' $SAMPLE_VCF \
| bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\n' \
| bedtools slop -g $GENOME -b 100 \
> $OUT/sample.bed

bcftools view -i 'INFO/SVTYPE="DEL" || INFO/SVTYPE="INS"' $BENCH \
| bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\n' \
| bedtools slop -g $GENOME -b 100 \
> $OUT/benchmark.bed

bedtools intersect -a $OUT/sample.bed -b $OUT/benchmark.bed -f 0.5 -r -u > $OUT/TP.bed
bedtools intersect -a $OUT/sample.bed -b $OUT/benchmark.bed -f 0.5 -r -v > $OUT/FP.bed
bedtools intersect -a $OUT/benchmark.bed -b $OUT/sample.bed -f 0.5 -r -v > $OUT/FN.bed
```

* The bedtools intersect command compares two variant files and identifies which variants overlap.
* When the sample file -a, the -v reports variants in the sample that do not overlap with the benchmark variants. These non-overlapping variants are considered False Positives, because they are detected in the sample but not present in the benchmark dataset.
* When the benchmark file -a, the -v reports variants in the benchmark that do not overlap with the sample variants. These variants are considered False Negatives, because they are present in the benchmark but were not detected in the sample dataset.
* The -f 0.5 -r option requires at least 50% reciprocal overlap, so both variants must overlap each other by at least 50%, allowing for small breakpoint differences.

## 6. Calculate the precision, recall and F1 score for indels for each sequencing technology (5pts)

* Recall = 13107 / (13107+337) = 13107/13444 = 97.5%
* F1 = 2 × (0.656 × 0.975) / (0.656 + 0.975) = 78.6%

* Precision = 4521 / (4521+2222) = 4521/6743 = 67.1%
* Recall = 4521 / (4521+8089) = 4521/12610 = 35.9%
* F1 = 2 × (0.671 × 0.359) / (0.671 + 0.359) = 46.6%

### ont

* Recall = 10129 / (10129+2498) = 10129/12627 = 80.2%
* F1 = 2 × (0.188 × 0.802) / (0.188 + 0.802) = 30.6%
